items.name: Frozen Butterbeer
items.description: A slushed version of the cream-soda-and-butterscotch drink, served with a thick foam head that sits on top rather than mixing in. Non-alcoholic, like every version of it.
items.verdict: The one to order. The cold version is sweet and thin by the third mouthful; the frozen version stays drinkable in Los Angeles heat, which is the whole argument.

items.name: Cold Butterbeer
items.description: The original version: a chilled cream soda base with a butterscotch foam poured over the top, served in a cup or a souvenir tankard.
items.verdict: Fine, and sweeter than most people expect. Order it in cool weather and order the frozen one otherwise. Buy it at the Hog's Head, not the outdoor cart, and save fifteen minutes.

items.name: Hot Butterbeer
items.description: The same butterscotch and cream soda flavor served warm, closer in texture to a hot custard drink than to the cold version.
items.verdict: Genuinely the best of the three on a cold night, and completely wrong in July. Southern California gives you maybe twenty evenings a year when this is the right order.

items.name: Fish and Chips
items.description: Battered white fish with thick-cut chips, served on a metal tray in the timber dining hall. The most consistently well-executed plate on the Three Broomsticks menu.
items.verdict: The order at Three Broomsticks. The batter holds, the fish is not overcooked, and it is the one item here that would pass without the theming to carry it.

items.name: Shepherd's Pie
items.description: Minced meat in gravy under a piped mashed potato crust, baked and served in its own dish with a side salad.
items.verdict: Solid, heavy and completely fine. It is the right order in January and a mistake in August, when you still have a hillside and four escalators ahead of you.

items.name: The Great Feast
items.description: A shared platter of rotisserie chicken, ribs, corn and potatoes intended for a family, sold as a single order rather than per person. Priced per platter and worth confirming at the counter.
items.verdict: Genuine value for four or more and a poor deal for two. Order it with a group and individual plates without one.

items.name: Hog's Head Brew
items.description: A draft beer brewed for Universal and sold only inside the Wizarding World, poured from the tap that sets off the animatronic hog's head above the bar.
items.verdict: A decent, unremarkable amber beer with a good trick attached. Worth ordering once for the tap gag, which most guests never see because they never come inside.

items.name: The Big Pink Donut
items.description: A plain cake donut roughly the size of a dinner plate, covered in pink frosting and sprinkles, sold under a statue of the mascot holding the same thing.
items.verdict: The most photographed food in the park and a mediocre donut. Buy one for the group, take the picture under the statue, and buy a standard glazed one if you actually want to eat a donut.

items.name: Glazed Donut
items.description: The standard-size donut sold alongside the enormous pink one, in glazed and a rotating set of other finishes.
items.verdict: Better than the Big Pink Donut and a third of the price, which is why almost nobody buys one. If you want a donut rather than a prop, this is the correct order.

items.name: Flaming Moe
items.description: A sweet orange-forward drink served in a tall souvenir glass over dry ice, so the whole thing smokes over the rim while you carry it. Available with or without alcohol.
items.verdict: You are buying an effect, not a cocktail, and it is worth it once. The non-alcoholic version is identical in every way that matters, which makes it the single most entertaining thing you can hand a child at this park.

items.name: Duff Beer
items.description: A real branded lager brewed for Universal rather than a prop, served at Moe's Tavern, the Duff Brewery bar outside and at Krusty Burger.
items.verdict: An ordinary lager with an extraordinary label. Drink it at Moe's, in the air conditioning, rather than standing in the sun at the outdoor bar paying the same money.

items.name: The Clogger
items.description: A deliberately excessive stacked burger built as a visual joke about American fast food, sold in a restaurant that is itself a joke about American fast food.
items.verdict: Order it if the absurdity is the point of your visit. Order a normal burger if you want lunch. It is not good, and it is not trying to be, and that is a defensible position for a menu item to take.

items.name: Krusty Burger
items.description: The standard burger on the menu: a single patty with cheese, lettuce, tomato and sauce, served with fries in themed packaging.
items.verdict: An entirely ordinary theme park burger in an entirely extraordinary room. Sixteen dollars is a lot for it, and you are partly paying for the air conditioning and the Krusty head outside.

items.name: Chicken and Waffle Sandwich
items.description: Fried chicken between two waffles instead of a bun, fried to order at the window rather than held under a lamp.
items.verdict: The best savory thing inside this park after Toadstool Cafe, and almost everyone walks past it to queue at Krusty Burger next door. Order this instead.

items.name: Taco Plate
items.description: A short order of tacos on corn tortillas from a themed truck parked on the Springfield street, with carne asada, chicken and a vegetarian option.
items.verdict: Unremarkable by any Los Angeles standard and a genuine relief by Springfield standards. The only thing in this area you can eat without needing a lie-down afterward.

items.name: Mario Bacon Cheeseburger
items.description: A bacon cheeseburger served under a bun shaped and colored as Mario's cap, plated with fries and presented on a themed tray.
items.verdict: The signature plate and, surprisingly, a properly cooked burger rather than a prop with meat in it. The kitchen here is doing real work behind the gimmick.

items.name: Super Mushroom Soup Bread Bowl
items.description: A cream of mushroom soup served inside a bread bowl baked and decorated to look like a Super Mushroom, red cap and white spots included.
items.verdict: The best-looking savory dish in the park and a genuinely decent soup underneath the presentation. The best vegetarian order inside these gates.

items.name: Question Block Tiramisu
items.description: A cube of tiramisu built and finished as a Mario question block, complete with the question mark on the face, served with a mushroom-shaped garnish.
items.verdict: The single best dessert inside this park and the rare themed item that people photograph and then finish. If you order one thing at Toadstool Cafe, order this.

items.name: Piranha Plant Caprese
items.description: A tomato and mozzarella salad arranged as a Piranha Plant emerging from a pipe, with basil and a green pesto base.
items.verdict: A properly conceived vegetarian dish rather than a substitution off a meat menu, which is rarer at this park than it should be. Light, which matters at lunchtime here.

items.name: Fire Flower Spaghetti and Meatballs
items.description: Spaghetti and meatballs in a spiced tomato sauce, plated with a fire-flower motif and served in a bowl rather than on a tray.
items.verdict: The least interesting plate on a strong menu, and still better than most of what this park serves. Order the burger or the soup ahead of it.

items.name: Super Star Lemon Squash
items.description: A sparkling lemon drink served with a star-shaped garnish, non-alcoholic and the most refreshing thing on the Toadstool Cafe menu.
items.verdict: Ten dollars for lemonade is a Universal Studios Hollywood price. It is genuinely good lemonade, and the cheapest way to sit in the best air-conditioned room in the park.

items.name: Chocolate Milkshake
items.description: A thick hand-spun milkshake served in a tall glass with the surplus in the metal cup alongside, the way a diner is supposed to do it.
items.verdict: The best thing on the Mel's menu by a distance and one of the better sweet items in the park. The burgers are ordinary; the shake is not.

items.name: Bacon Cheeseburger
items.description: A straightforward diner burger with bacon and cheese, served with fries in a chrome-and-vinyl room near the park entrance.
items.verdict: Competent and unmemorable. You are really paying for an air-conditioned booth close to the gate, which at this park is a fair enough thing to pay for.

items.name: Fried Chicken Plate
items.description: Bone-in fried chicken with sides, served in the large themed dining rooms next to Despicable Me Minion Mayhem.
items.verdict: Above the park average and generously portioned, which is the most you can reasonably ask of a Minion-branded restaurant. A sensible default lunch on the Upper Lot.

items.name: Minion Mac and Cheese
items.description: A baked macaroni cheese served in a themed dish, with a crumb topping and enough of it to work as a shared side.
items.verdict: The reliable order for a child who will not eat anything else, and a decent vegetarian option in a park short of them. Nothing to write home about, and nothing wrong with it.

items.name: Banana Cream Dessert
items.description: A layered banana cream dessert in a themed vessel, part of the banana program that a Minion restaurant was never going to avoid.
items.verdict: The desserts are the part of this kitchen that clearly enjoys itself, and this is the best of them. Better than the savory food it follows.

items.name: Cinnamon Sugar Churro
items.description: The standard fried dough stick rolled in cinnamon sugar, sold from carts at several points around the Upper Lot.
items.verdict: A fine churro at roughly fifty percent more than the same thing costs at Disneyland down the freeway. Buy one from a cart that is actively frying, or do not bother.

items.name: Smoked Turkey Leg
items.description: An enormous cured and smoked turkey leg from a cart on the Upper Lot, eaten standing up with nothing that could reasonably be called a napkin.
items.verdict: It tastes like ham, because of the curing, and that surprises everyone. Share one across the group as a novelty rather than buying it as lunch.

items.name: Cold Brew Coffee
items.description: A standard Starbucks cold brew from the Upper Lot location, priced the same as it is anywhere else in Los Angeles.
items.verdict: The best value purchase inside this park, entirely because it is the only one not carrying a theme park markup. Unglamorous and genuinely useful.

items.name: Breakfast Sandwich
items.description: A standard warmed Starbucks breakfast sandwich, with egg and cheese versions available alongside the meat ones.
items.verdict: This park has almost no real breakfast offering inside the gate, and this is the practical answer. Not a recommendation so much as an admission.

items.name: Smoked Ribs Plate
items.description: A half rack of smoked ribs with sides, served at the Lower Lot's only substantial restaurant next to Jurassic World.
items.verdict: Ordinary barbecue in the one place where that hardly matters, because the alternative is four escalators each way. Eat it and stay down here.

items.name: Grilled Chicken Plate
items.description: Grilled chicken with rice and vegetables, the lightest main course available on the Lower Lot.
items.verdict: The sensible order if you are riding Jurassic World afterward, which you probably are. The ribs are better and considerably worse timed.

items.name: Mac and Cheese
items.description: A baked macaroni cheese served as a main or a side, and effectively the only vegetarian main on the Lower Lot.
items.verdict: Adequate, and the only real vegetarian option on this level of the park. That is a criticism of the Lower Lot rather than of the dish.

items.name: Frozen Tropical Cocktail
items.description: A blended rum-based tropical drink from the covered bar beside Jurassic World, served in a plastic cup or a souvenir vessel for considerably more.
items.verdict: Sweet, strong and correctly timed. Coming off Jurassic World soaked and sitting in the shade with one of these is among the better twenty minutes available here.

items.name: Cold Brew Coffee
items.description: The same standard Starbucks cold brew, from the Lower Lot location that most guests do not know exists.
items.verdict: Listed because knowing it is here is worth more than the drink is. It is the reason you never need to take the escalators up for a coffee.
